newsitem.title: ITALY: World Bank to send mission to Albania by end April.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to send mission to Albania by end April.

text.p: The World Bank will send a mission to Albania by the end of the month to assess how much money is needed for reconstruction projects in the troubled Balkan nation, a bank official said on Monday.

The mission will examine the damage caused to Albanian infrastructure by weeks of armed unrest in which some 300 people have died, Franco Passacantando, a World Bank executive director, told a conference on Albania.
But Passacantando added that the World Bank would not reimburse the thousands of Albanian families who lost money when pyramid investment schemes collapsed earlier this year.

The World Bank has already set aside financing for health work and projects to rebuild homes and schools destroyed by weeks of anarchy that followed the failure of the savings schemes, Passacantando said. He did not give precise details.
Some of the other reconstruction projects should also be financed by Albania's private sector, which is still largely operative, Passacantando said.
"In helping Albania, it is important not to create disincentives for a private system which is already able to sponsor activities," he said in a speech.
